text:
- chief complaint: the patient presents for evaluation of a newly diagnosed ovarian cancer, with severe pain and bleeding as presenting symptoms.
- history of present illness: the patient has a past medical history of type 2 diabetes and was referred after an abdominal CT showed a 3 cm left ovarian mass with localized lymph node involvement and no gross peritoneal or metastatic disease. Presenting symptoms were severe pain and bleeding. The patient reports no vomiting. The patient reports no history of pregnancy or children, menarche at age 13, and menopause at age 28, and does not take hormone replacement therapy. The patient has no history of endometriosis. Family history is unknown due to adoption.
- physical examination: slight left lower quadrant tenderness without rebound or guarding; palpable left adnexal mass; no right-sided mass; external genitalia and vaginal vault normal; cervix pink without lesions.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: severe pain, bleeding, constipation, weight loss, feeling depressed; no vomiting.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A.
- follow-up instructions: blood tests (CA-125, hCG, AFP, LDH); genetic counseling and testing; surgery (hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, lymph node dissection, tissue sampling), followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with cisplatin and taxol, possibly intraperitoneal chemotherapy; final pathology report pending for definitive staging.
